details:
When using Camera Dolly in Multi Streaming mode with multiple paths set to Local (IsLocal), only one path's camera reflects the player's real-time positional movement in its Spout output (OBS). The other paths' cameras animate along their defined paths correctly, but do NOT update their local position offset based on the player's actual movement.

When the currently "active" path finishes its cycle, the next path's camera suddenly snaps/teleports to account for all accumulated player movement at once, then continues its path animation from the corrected position. This creates a jarring "hook" jump in the Spout output visible in OBS.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Open Camera, switch to Stream mode, enable Spout Stream

2. Switch Dolly mode to Multi

3. Create 3-4 paths with IsLocal points

4. Set Looping to Reverse, Streaming to Multi

5. Press Play

6. Move your character around the world while the dolly is playing

7. Observe in OBS: Only one VRCSender (the currently "primary" path) shows the player's movement reflected in real-time

8. Other VRCSenders show the camera animating along its path, but the player appears stationary (no local position offset applied)

9. When the primary path cycle ends and transitions to the next path, that camera suddenly jumps to the player's actual current position

Expected Behavior:

All paths' cameras should simultaneously reflect the player's real-time local position changes in their Spout output, since they are all set to Local space.

Actual Behavior:

Only one path at a time applies the player's positional delta to its Spout output. Others accumulate the delta internally but do not render it until they become the "primary" path.

Environment:

- VRChat latest live build (2026.2.3+)

- Windows 11, RTX 5090, OBS 32.2.1 with win-spout plugin

- VR mode (Quest Pro via Air Link)

Related issues:

title: [Dolly] Multi-stream mode: Only one path reflects player local position in real-time via Spout output
